photo.caption: Dating from 1375, the full 8 sheet Catalan Atlas made by Abraham Cresques, cartographer to King Pere IV of Aragon. It was a gift from the King of the Crown of Aragon to the King of France. Many later maps and "portolan charts" are copies of this original Catalan one.
photo.description: Atlas from the 14th century attributed to Abraham Cresques.

photo.caption: A pre-Mercator nautical chart of 1571, from Portuguese cartographer Fernão Vaz Dourado (c. 1520–c. 1580). It belongs to the so-called plane chart model, where observed latitudes and magnetic directions are plotted directly into the plane, with a constant scale, as if the Earth were plane (Portuguese National Archives of Torre do Tombo, Lisbon).
photo.description: Nautical chart of Portuguese cartographer Fernão Vaz Dourado (c. 1520 - c. 1580), part of a nautical atlas drawn in 1571 and now kept in the Portuguese National Archives of Torre do Tombo (ANTT), Lisbon.
photo.date: Original work of 1571. Photo taken in 2008

photo.caption: Portolan chart by Jorge de Aguiar (1492), the oldest known signed and dated chart of Portuguese origin (Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, University of Yale, New Haven, USA)
photo.description: Reproduction of Jorge de Aguiar's chart of the Mediterranean, Western Europe and African Coast (1492). Size of the original: 1030 × 770 mm.
